An Introduction To Wordcasting
This work has notes in nearly every margin, penned in several languages, clearly having exchanged hands several times over the decades.

Most spellcasters spend their entire careers learning and mastering the spells that make up their calling, but there is another way. Some turn their backs on the rote memorization and formulae that traditional spellcasters use to create magic, and instead unlock the power behind the spells themselves, the fundamental building blocks of magic. Such a spellcaster learns the words of power, and through them, learns to control the very forces underlying magic, shaping and wielding them like no other.

Words of power represent a primal form of magic used in ages past. As such, use of the words of power system is rare these days, and its practitioners tend to be masters of esoteric lore. Words of power constitute a root system, from which all modern magic descends. Although powerful, this system is more primitive in some ways than modern magic. Flexible, but lacking the refinement of modern spells, this system allows spellcasters to shape magic in ways they never could before, while simultaneously preventing them from producing the same sort of incredibly specific effects that ordinary spellcasters master.

It is not surprising that most magical institutions and centers for learning treat words of power as an archaic art, to be studied along with other historical matters, but not actually practiced. Those who delve into the lore of words of power often find themselves lost in an ancient art that they alone might now know. There is power there, but each wordcaster must find it alone.
Atropus is Nigh
A faded recounting of a segment of an apocalyptic prophet's sermon.

Atropus is nigh! The World Born Dead! Its coming can only mean doom! Watch for the signs! The undead spontaneously rising! The return of the raveners! Atropus will lay waste to Toril as it did Glyth! With the fall of the valorous, none left can oppose the coming of the undead primordial!
The Fall of the Valorous
This journal is redolent with the fetid odor of death and decay.

I should have seen the signs - the flocks of strange birds, the blackening of the sacred waters, the spasms of pain that blossomed in my chest when I held aloft my holy symbol - such dark tidings could only mean death. Were I wiser, perhaps I would have sought the counsel of the Grand Inquisitor or delivered a warning to the Conclave in Baldur's Gate. But nay, I was foolhardy; I put too much faith in the power of the Inquisition.

The Valor Inquisition has fallen. My Sending spells fall on deaf ears, and my divinations and scrying return naught but the inky blackness of the void. My hope that one among us yet lives grows thinner with each passing day. I worry now that I alone must carry the burden of remembrance.

This must have been the work of the raveners. Whispers in the dark corners of the world spoke of a new Ravener King, one under whom the raveners would rally and mobilize. It was a grim fortune indeed that we should have fallen to ruin at the hands of those blasphemous abominations, on the precipice of a miraculous breakthrough. Had we only a bit more time, perhaps we could have perfected the Holy Words, the divine oration that is anathema to these minions of evil.

I, Taarogus Dantill, Vindicator of the Valorous and Shining Knight of the Ravener Hunters, entrust to you this mission:

Seek out the Holy Words, the bane of raveners.
Learn the truth of the fall of the Valorous, and lay to rest their weary souls.
Slay the Ravener King and ensure his forces may never again threaten the sanctity of the Material Plane.

I have nothing to offer you but a Holy Word of my own design. With it, you may yet stand strong against the tides of darkness. Should I survive, I will return here once I know the divine oration is in safe hands.

May the gods watch over your battles, friend.
Folly of our Forebears
This crisp note is poked through in several places, having become the target of the writer's frustrations.

Taarogus has forbidden the use of divination and communication magic between outposts, claiming the “Ravener King” might intercept our correspondence, learn of our plots, and dispatch his forces to destroy us. The thought that a dragon - a solitary beast with pride like none other - would bend its knee and mobilize among others is laughable at best. At worst, the very implication calls into question Taarogus' ability to lead.

I believe I have deduced the location of two of our other research sites. One is the Emerald Grove - of this I am certain. Saelethil and Selene are performing animal experiments with the aid of the druids. Selene, ever sanctimonious, chided me for breaking the communication ban, but why should I care? She's just as culpable for responding.

It is the second location of which I am less certain - Crèche Y'llek. Those xenophobes must be in dire straits indeed to accept an offer to collaborate with Daregrir. If my deduction is correct, either Siovril has a silvered tongue like none other, or the githyanki have witnessed firsthand the ravener threat and know that they're out of their depth. As are we all, unfortunately, but such is the folly of our forebears for believing the raveners could never return and sinking into complacency.
In Need of an Iconoclast
A missive penned in elegant script, bearing the seal of the Vengeance Inquisition.

Iconoclasts, one and all:

I have identified an intimation of the Grand Inquisitor's whereabouts - a mithral amulet secreted away in the Underdark. This insidious thing is cursed beyond all imagination; my celestial sight nearly failed to penetrate its illusory ward. To the best of my ability, I have drawn here the sigils I can interpret, though their very presence is anathema to every fiber of my being.

I understand that we have fallen upon dark times and the Spellkiller Inquisition has all but disbanded. Nevertheless, I prithee make haste to my encampment, for I wither at the malignity this amulet exudes that draws ever closer to my heart and soul.

Should I be dispatched when you arrive, leave as much information as you can muster and, if you cannot break the curse, I will do what I must to see this mission through to the end.

Faithfully,
Naldrase Elsidyi
Inquisitions of Faerûn
A brief description of the inquisitions active across Faerûn and their missions.

Damnation: The prospect of an afterlife filled with torment can cause even the most stalwart to blanch - at least for a moment. The Damned employ hellish magics and, occasionally, the services of devils to intimidate their enemies into submission.

Fate: Fate is a powerful tool for those who dole out justice for their deity. The Fateful can read the strands of fate, and those strands guide their endeavors.

Illumination: Many times an inquisitor's greatest strength is pure and unflinching illumination; errors are often illuminated by the light and wisdom of the Luminous.

Order: Most inquisitors fight insane aberrations and demonic creatures as well as the chaos of heresy. The Harmonic use the dictum and the mantles of law in order to aid their struggle.

Redemption: For some, their deity inspires them with hope that wayward members of their faith can be brought back into the fold. Redeemers reach out to their misguided fellows and give them every chance to turn back from conflict with the true faith, even if their differences come to violence.

Truth: Evil often hides itself behind a mask of good. The Truthful are experts at ferreting out those who are not what they seem, and use their powers to reveal the true forms of the unworthy.

Valor: It takes courage to confront the enemies of your faith. There is no monster too menacing nor duty too daunting for one of the Valorous.
It Is What Must Be Done
Inscribed on the inside of the front cover reads, "To Adrasteia, my love eternal. May your journeys take you far and wide, and may you be returned to my loving embrace before long."

Oh, how weary I grow answering the same questions over and over. These Valorous must start implementing basic history lessons as part of their onboarding. For their many strengths, intelligence is not chief among them. Let us only hope that history will not repeat itself before darkness comes to pass.

As a converted Zealot, I must put ink to parchment and set the record straight. The inquisitions of Zeal and Valor were once one - the Ardor Inquisition. Things started off well enough, but as time went on, the differences in the (now) two factions became more pronounced.

“Zealots,” as we term those of the Zeal Inquisition, are absolutely devoted to their ideals. Zeal itself is extreme enthusiasm, passion, and fervor aimed at a cause or objective. To be a Zealot is not to be sure of oneself but to be sure of the cause one serves. The “Valorous,” rather than being devoted to a more singular, specific cause, fashion themselves after the concepts of bravery and virtue. They have full faith in themselves, not because they are vain and proud, but because they know that it is simply how it must be.

A Zealot's style of combat can be termed reckless by some, as they wholeheartedly jump into the fray, seemingly with no regard for their well-being. However, this is not the case. A zeal inquisitor simply places their ultimate faith in the cause they serve and knows that through this devotion their victory is assured. Where Zealots acknowledge risk, throw caution to the wind, and trust in their faith to preserve them, the Valorous simply do not register risk. Whether consciously or otherwise, a valor inquisitor almost can't afford to acknowledge risk, lest they find themselves faltering in the face of death.

Due to their reputation for being fearless, the Valorous typically find themselves facing off against seemingly insurmountable odds. The Valorous fight on, not for glory nor devotion, but simply because it is what must be done.
Lamentations
The mephitic and miasmic vitriol of the swamp has seeped into this unadorned note, charging it with palpable and unadulterated loathing.

Why must we have been burdened so?

Curse our predecessors for their negligence and confound the Grand Inquisitor for his hubris!

The Harmonic were right, but we were too arrogant and cocksure to listen. They foresaw the only logical outcome of our laxity and now we suffer the most dire of consequences. Had Siovril only shut his mouth and accepted the truth, perhaps our progress with the Holy Words could have been expedited.

And I'd not be rotting here in this gods-forsaken swamp, withering away alone and destitute.

Whosoever should read my dying words, do take solace in knowing that I am tormenting the Grand Inquisitor eternally in the Hells.
Missive to Qynoth
This tightly-furled scroll exudes an unpleasant aura, almost as though it does not want to be read.

Qynoth,

To address our last correspondence - while it is no doubt a harsh vicissitude that Taarogus has lost his faithful trio of glorified underlings amidst our progress with the Divine Oration, it does not excuse his irrational behavior. These unnecessary complications are hindering our progress more than they are helping to ward us from this mythical “Ravener King.” I don't know from where such childish delusions could have spawned, but they must be put to an end. I did not assign you as his ward for your virtue, nor for your might, but for your eloquence. Given enough time, I believe you may be able to help Taarogus move past his misgivings.

Our trials are proving fortuitous, supplanting previous findings from the Arcane Tower. Not to say their work is without merit, but our progress would be greatly expedited if Adrasteia could be moved to the Emerald Grove, and Selene to the Crèche.

However, more pressing than our research - the Grand Inquisitor seems to have vanished. Unfortunately, Taarogus' insanity spread to Siovril, and he ventured off on a fool's errand in search of red herrings. He bade us keep our research secret from one another, lest the Ravener King catch wind of our findings and dispatch his legions upon us. Ever cryptic, as is the wont of the Fateful - “Whence tolls extolled and the wicked disguise themselves in the coats of the just, Iovru's chill wind heralds Veizoadeoth, and all becomes dust.” Do with this what you will, for I am quite tired of it all.

Vogrevol
Notes on the Ravener's Frightful Presence
A scroll covered in intricate drawings and divine wards, detailing an inquisitor's research findings.

Interestingly, though not surprisingly, beasts of all varieties will make every effort to avoid the ravener. With the aid of the druids, we performed many experiments to attempt to coax animals anywhere near the ravener. Nothing short of magical coercion—which we were loath to attempt—could persuade these creatures nearer than 9 meters, roughly.

Though I should record it here for posterity, I would much rather forget the dreadful things these animals conveyed to us through druidic magic. A great burden weighs on my heart as I witness how these gentle creatures have been irrevocably altered by the mere presence of the ravener. If I should never again have the misfortune of encountering one, I will consider myself blessed beyond measure.

We needn't perform tests with humanoid subjects, as the conclusion seems clear—the ravener exudes an aura of terror, striking fear into the very souls of those whose will cannot withstand the dread of the endless void. Further research will be aimed at combating this aura.
On the Nature of Soul Wards
A note covered in intricate drawings and arcane formulae, detailing an inquisitor's research findings.

... Of significant note is what we have termed the “soul ward,” an intangible field of siphoned soul energy that protects a ravener from destruction. No two raveners manifest their soul wards in quite the same way. Some soul wards infuse the ravener with a shadowy aura, others with the screaming spirits of the dead. Some raveners lack a visible soul ward entirely, making that part of themselves invisible to deny their opponents a complete understanding of their defenses. The energy contained within the soul ward fuels the ravener's arcane power, guards the ravener from harm, and sustains its unliving existence. A ravener deprived of the ability to refresh its soul ward must carefully hoard its magical energy, and should it be denied victims, it slowly deteriorates and grows vulnerable, eventually crumbling to dust—though few come close to that point, with the all-consuming hunger of the empty ward driving them to death in battle long before soul starvation sets in.

It is imperative that no living creature die in close proximity to the ravener. Death fuels their soul ward like nothing else, rending the unfortunate soul from its host body. Nothing short of divine intervention can bring back these lost souls.

Through considerable sacrifice, we have nearly refined the divine oration to weaken the soul ward for a short period of time, during which all measures should be taken to ensure the ravener is exterminated.
Preservation
Each quill stroke on this scrap of parchment was penned slowly and with great care, almost as though the writer did not want to finish it.

Khionzu,

Surely you must realize that our defeat is all but assured? We are outnumbered, outwitted, outclassed and out of our depth. Persevere if you must, but I am taking matters into my own hands. The Valor Inquisition must not be forgotten.

A foul creature lurks below, its inception brought about by sinister fanaticism. I will face it alone, as is what must be done.

I do hope you'll join me, though.
Ravener Malevolence: Human Case Study #4
This journal, detailing an inquisitor's research findings, is covered in intricate drawings and emanates an aura of great evil.

We herein define a ravener's malevolence as the ill effects resulting from their claws and breath weapon. This manifests chiefly as a loss of one's life force; the erosion of their soul is compounded by progressive supernatural deterioration of their mind and body.

Day 1: Subject does not exhibit any symptoms as described in the Compendia Maleficus. Ravener shows no signs of improvement.

Day 2: Subject mentioned sleeping poorly, with dreams of a starless sky that absorbed all sound and light. Ravener shows no signs of improvement.

Day 3: Subject is visibly fatigued - sunken eyes, sluggish movement, difficulty forming complete thoughts. The subject spoke at length of a vivid nightmare wherein they remotely viewed their own body falling into a bottomless pit. The pit spoke in a language that the subject had not heard. The subject awoke bleeding from both ears and with black saliva pooled on the ground beneath them. Ravener has begun weakly gnawing at its enclosure. We reject the hypothesis that the strength of a ravener's malevolence is tied to their physical well-being.

Day 4: Subject is incapable of rising from their bed. Their skin has paled so intensely as to be near-translucent. The subject cannot speak save for the simplest of phrases. Divination magic revealed that the subject's thoughts are devoid of any abstraction or conceptualization, and are focused solely on how their “heart feels cold.” Ravener again emanates the frightful presence of which we were warned by the Emerald Grove. We accept the hypothesis that a ravener's malevolence directly empowers their Soul Ward.

Day 4, Entry 2: Subject has died, their face contorted in pure terror. Our cleric was left dumbfounded by the absence of a soul, without which they cannot anchor a revival spell. Ravener has escaped its enclosure and is currently at large. We accept the hypothesis that a ravener's malevolence separates one's soul from their physical form.
Ruination
The last words of a crestfallen inquisitor.

Khionzu is dead. The raveners got her. She was nigh more than a husk when I found her. May the divines rest her soul.

The beast is far too powerful to face alone. There is no one left. Whosoever should read this, if you possess the strength, slay the beast and sanctify my body. Even in death I will persevere to pass on the secrets of valor.
Saelethil's Ailment
A hastily-scrawled note of great importance to those who read closely.

Saelethil has taken to acting strangely as of late, as though possessed. Others might not notice it, but as we've been working together so closely in recent months, I can tell there is something sinister afoot. Behind their vacant stare screams a trapped soul, begging to be released from its captivity.

In the still of the night I hear them whispering to unseen visitors. They speak of the Ravener King, of Atropus, and the lands overrun with undead under a sunless sky. This is no ordinary despair - if the Ravener King truly exists, Saelethil must have glimpsed but a sliver of his twisted mind.

The Word of Resolve is our only recourse. Should their will prove strong, I believe it can break Saelethil from the grasp of the Ravener King.
Saelethil's Farewell
This tattered note is redolent with the fetid odor of death and decay.

We cannot win. I use what little agency that remains to tell you this: it is utterly hopeless. Raveners will claim the earth and Atropus will claim the sky. The Ravener King erodes my mind, turning my thoughts to his dark whims. Beyond the quill with which I write this valedictory is a purgatory everlasting. Atropus is nigh.
Someone Come Move This Thing
A somewhat interesting, mildly adorned note.

I called in a favor from Z to have him explain what I'm looking at here. Some kind of divine magic, if I understood his explanation. Some Selûnite inquisitors in the Underdark came up with it. We can't get past it because we “aren't holy enough.” Go figure. Z says we oughta go on some kind of holy pilgrimage to prove that we're good enough. That old shrine to Cahoot oughta suffice, eh?

Or not. Avernus isn't hot enough for some of you bastards.

How the hells did you even move this thing in here
Speculations of an Iconoclast
A set of notes covered in arcane diagrams, divine scripture, and invocations of a multitude of otherworldly beings.

Prayers alone have been insufficient in assuaging the voices. We need some kind of divine focus component - intelligence suggests there are multiple idols in the region that may serve as a powerful enough focus for a deific invocation.

Most insidious is the localized antimagic field upon the amulet. It craves life essence, and as such we must wear the amulet to disable the field. The volunteer receives reduced effects from our restorations, yet claims to feel more attuned to the curse with each application of curative magics. However, our progress seems to be coming at the expense of his sanity. Perhaps at the expense of all of our sanity, as I too feel as though I hear the sinister whispers of a power far beyond our comprehension.
Treatise on the Viandrioth Culling
A dense tome detailing a pivotal event in the history of the Valor Inquisition.

[The following is an excerpt from a larger work regarding the history of the Valor Inquisition and their crusades against the Viandrioth clan of raveners.]

In 1064 DR, the Ravener Hunters, led by Grand Inquisitor Hyphos of the Illumination Inquisition, launched the first offensive of the Viandrioth Culling against General Xaerliedys. The offensive made heavy use of light-based divine magic, as raveners of this age were famously weak to sunlight. Aided by a small company of lantern archons, the Ravener Hunters (themselves a small company of the Valorous tasked with spearheading the Culling) engaged with Xaerliedys' undead forces at the Ruins of Dharmagongh in Murghôm.

After 6 days and 6 nights, Xaerliedys was slain and the Murghôm raveners routed. However, the strain of the conflict was too much for Hyphos to bear at his age, and he fell shortly thereafter. Siovril of the Valorous, a hero of the offensive, was named Grand Inquisitor at Hyphos' funeral.

These events would largely set the tone for the remainder of the Viandrioth Culling - ultimately positive in favor of the Valorous, but with significant losses at the hands of the undead menace.
The Unholy Communion of Dragons and Unlife
This tome, detailing an inquisitor's research findings, is covered in intricate drawings and pulsates faintly with necromantic energies.

As undead creatures, a ravener's ability to experience sensations is irrevocably dulled. Their hearing and vision may be peerless, but becoming a ravener demands the sacrifice of the nuances of taste, scent, and even touch, along with countless other pleasures of life. As a result, the ravener thrives on horrific excesses of emotion, for only in the heat of battle and wanton destruction or the gluttonous consumption of souls does the ravener again come close to the glorious sensations of being a living dragon.

Even the most successful ravener transformation comes with a terrible price, as all of the living dragon's natural magical abilities are burned away in an instant in the explosion of necromantic energies. In its place, negative energy floods in to infuse and enhance the ravener's breath weapon, fuel their magical powers, and even sustain the creature's ability to fly on skeletal wings.

Raveners are self-made undead, not created or generated spontaneously in the fashion of weaker undead. As such, their nature reflects the circumstances of their transformation. Careless adventurers may well mistake a ravener for a mere draconic skeleton or zombie, an error few survive. Once reborn, raveners are effectively immortal, though this immortality is not without a terrible price. The arcane void within a ravener's heart leaves them consumed by a maddening craving, a hunger that can only be sated by the life-essence of other beings. Each soul devoured temporarily restores a precious sliver of the draconic magic sacrificed to overcome the ravener's mortality. But all too soon, the need to feast returns.
Valor Outposts of the Sword Coast
This ancient map is faded, but the insignia of the Valor Inquisition is still clearly visible.
This map of the Sword Coast is worn and frail, yet clearly depicts the locations of three outposts of the Valor Inquisition along the Chionthar and environs of Elturel.
The Valorous Virtues
This enchiridion bears the faintest traces of divine magic woven into every word.

So named due to their popularization by T. Dantill of the Valor Inquisition, the Valorous Virtues are a set of 5 ideals of which knights of the realm should strive to embody. It is said that adherence to the Valorous Virtues strengthens one's ties to their deity and to themselves, empowering their resolve and cementing them as a paragon of chivalry.

A knight possessing Valor does not hesitate to stand against the majority, nor do they shy away from acts requiring bravery and heroism.

A knight of Honor stands behind their actions, holds fast to their morals and convictions, and faces every challenge head-on.

A knight with Compassion never turns a blind eye to misfortune, and always stands in defense of the wronged.

A knight possessing Generosity never lets others go without - they share their prosperity with others and let their allies want for nothing.

Wisdom is a virtue which one should strive to cultivate throughout their life. A wise choice is not always the simple choice nor the easy choice, but to possess Wisdom is to make the choices that make one better.
Veiled In Death's Shroud
This letter, bearing the insignia of the Valor Inquisition, is neatly folded and addressed directly to you.

Whether this letter reaches you by my hand or by my corpse, I thank you for freeing me from the chains of servitude. My dearest companions, however, were not so fortunate as to have escaped the clutches of the Ravener King. I fear that my insurgent actions against the Ravener King sparked his ire, which he exacted upon my allies. Prithee, find my faithful compatriots:

Naldrase Elsidyi, the Archon of Justice
Zinia Kalyphise, the Harbinger of Harmony
Xandril Felgorn, the Bulwark of the Righteous

And free them from the clutches of evil.

Should I yet live, I will begin the hunt as well. In life or death, I hope our paths may cross once more.

Yours faithfully,
Taarogus Dantill
Word of Power
Holy Words
Speak into existence the divine language that you have acquired on your journey.
Apostle of the Holy Word

To speak a Word of Power is to invite a primal, volatile current of magic into your body, mind, and soul. Their power comes with a price:

Your AC is reduced by 1. For every 2 Holy Words you learn beyond this, your AC is reduced by an additional 1. For every 2 Holy Words you learn, all of your Saving Throws are reduced by 1.

Activating this toggle while in combat will Stun you for one round, as the overwhelming power of the Holy Words floods your mind.
Must be an Apostle of the Holy Word.
Vaelythra
Word of Soothing
You whisper a word of repose that soothes and heals your allies. You restore [1] per point of your Wisdom <LSTag Tooltip="AbilityModifier">Modifier</LSTag> to the target.
Lulix
Word of Brilliance

You utter a divine word and burning radiance erupts from you.

Dragons, fiends and undead have Disadvantage on their Saving Throws.
Arzimyr
Word of Resolve

Your battle cry rouses the target to stand steadfast in the heat of battle. The target gains <LSTag Tooltip="Advantage">Advantage</LSTag> on <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag> against <LSTag Tooltip="CharmedGroup">Charmed</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FRIGHTENED">Frightened</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="POISONED">Poisoned</LSTag>, and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="RESTRAINED">Restrained</LSTag> conditions, and is freed from any <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="PARALYZED">Paralysis</LSTag> or <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="STUNNED">Stun</LSTag> effects.
Arzimyr's Resolve

Has <LSTag Tooltip="Advantage">Advantage</LSTag> on <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throws</LSTag> against <LSTag Tooltip="CharmedGroup">Charmed</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="FRIGHTENED">Frightened</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="POISONED">Poisoned</LSTag>, and <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="RESTRAINED">Restrained</LSTag> conditions.
Grants immunity to a ravener's Frightful Presence.
Xulvorith
Word of Penance
With a muttered curse, all damage dealt by the target during the duration of Word of Penance is dealt back to them as[1] when the spell expires.
Xulvorith's Damnation
Damage dealt by this entity while this status is active is dealt back to them as[1] when the status expires.
Target's soul is held captive by a ravener.
Target must be an ally.
Must take a Short Rest.
Must take a Long Rest.
Undead Dragon Traits

As both an undead and a dragon, a ravener exhibits the following traits: Immunity to Bleeding, Blindness, Charm, Disease, Fear, Paralysis, Poison, Sleep, Stunn, and nonlethal damage, as well as Advantage on saving throws against being Turned.

Raveners calculate their hit points and Constitution-based Saving Throws using Charisma, and add half of their Charisma Modifier as a bonus to their AC.

Raveners have Blindsight and can see through magical darkness and fog.
Degenerating Strikes

Raveners score a Critical Hit when rolling an 18 or higher. On a Critical Hit, targets must pass a Constitution Saving Throw or be afflicted by a Negative Level.

Raveners add 5 points to their Soul Ward when afflicting a creature with a Negative Level from their melee attacks.

Raveners add 1 point to their Soul Ward per Negative Level inflicted by their Breath of Malevolence.
Ravener's Desecration

Cursed by the vile energies of a ravener, this blighted aura harms all who dare get close.

Can be cleansed with Consecrate or sufficient[1].
Ravener's Rot
Your vitality is being drained by the malevolent energies of a ravener.
Ravener's Consumption

Entity's soul is consumed by a ravener.

Can be cleansed with Vaelythra, but not while the ravener that consumed the entity's soul yet lives.
Ignores Resistance and Immunity
Lash out with deadly claws, potentially causing your target to <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="JL_FOTV_RAVENER_CLAWBLEED">Hemorrhage</LSTag>.
Ravenous Hemorrhage

Takes damage at the start of each turn and has Disadvantage on Constitution Saving Throws.

Can be removed by healing, but the healer must pass a DC 20 Saving Throw using their Spellcasting Ability or fail to stop the bleeding.
Bite a target, potentially draining their <LSTag Tooltip="Constitution">Constitution</LSTag> by 1.
Ravenous Decay: Constitution

Ravener King's Command

The Ravener King will not lose his favorite minion so easily. Taarogus receives the benefits of <LSTag Type="Passive" Tooltip="JL_FOTV_Ravener_DegeneratingStrikes_Taarogus">Degenerating Strikes</LSTag>, <LSTag Type="Passive" Tooltip="JL_FOTV_Ravener_FrightfulPresence_Taarogus">Frightful Presence</LSTag>, and <LSTag Type="Passive" Tooltip="JL_FOTV_Ravener_DivineDefiance_Taarogus">Divine Defiance</LSTag>.

Those under the Ravener King's Command score a <LSTag Tooltip="CriticalHit">Critical Hit</LSTag> when rolling an 18 or higher. On a Critical Hit, targets must pass a Constitution <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throw</LSTag> or be afflicted by a <LSTag Type="Status" Tooltip="JL_FOTV_NEGATIVELEVEL">Negative Level</LSTag>.

Those under the Ravener King's Command emanate an aura of fear. The first time you enter this entity's Frightful Presence, you must pass a Wisdom Saving Throw or be afflicted by Ravener's Dread for as long as you are within [1] of the entity.

This entity deals an additional [2] to enemies that they have afflicted with their dreadful presence.

Those under the Ravener King's Command are resilient to magic from divine sources. You must pass a <LSTag Tooltip="SavingThrow">Saving Throw</LSTag> with your <LSTag Tooltip="SpellcastingAbility">Spellcasting Ability</LSTag> or fail to affect this entity with your divine magic.

When Downed, the DC of Death Saving Throws is increased to 15, and you are allowed only 2 failures before death.

When brought back from death, your maximum hit points are reduced by your character level. This effect can stack.

If you reach 0 hit points, you fall Unconscious and must make Death Saving Throws. On 3 successes, you stop bleeding out and become Stable. On 2 failures, you die.
